blocks.text: Questions on what this page has just taught. Choose one answer for each.

questions.stem: Per this page, which conversion needs a piece of information that the value being converted does not carry?

options.text: OffsetDateTime to ZonedDateTime, which needs the region the offset belongs to
options.says: The page says going from OffsetDateTime to ZonedDateTime requires specifying which zone the offset belongs to.

options.text: ZonedDateTime to OffsetDateTime, which needs the offset in force at that time
options.says: The page calls ZonedDateTime to OffsetDateTime lossless via toOffsetDateTime(): the zone already knows its offset.

options.text: ZonedDateTime to Instant, which needs the zone the instant is read in
options.says: The page's examples call toInstant() with no argument; a ZonedDateTime already names its point on the timeline.

questions.stem: Per this page, what does `ZoneId.of("CST")` do?

options.text: It returns America/Chicago, the Central Standard Time zone
options.says: The page says only ZoneId.of("CST", ZoneId.SHORT_IDS) resolves CST to America/Chicago; the plain call does not.

options.text: It returns Asia/Shanghai, the China Standard Time zone
options.says: The page names China Standard Time only as the other meaning that makes CST ambiguous; nothing resolves CST to Shanghai.

options.text: It throws ZoneRulesException for an unknown time-zone ID
options.says: The page shows this call throwing ZoneRulesException, and says to use IANA IDs such as America/Chicago.

origin.section: Common Pitfalls and How to Avoid Them

concepts: Three-letter abbreviations such as CST are ambiguous and ZoneId.of refuses them; IANA region IDs name a zone.
ZonedDateTime to OffsetDateTime is lossless, while OffsetDateTime to ZonedDateTime needs the zone the offset belongs to.
